new: In the LXX regularly (Thackeray *Gr.* i. p. 183) and in the Κοινή frequently, especially in the Ptolemaic period, πρῶτος stands for πρότερος, so reversing the usual Hellenistic rule that the comparative does duty for both degrees of comparison.
